briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Rescheduling Momentum Builds Nationally While Michigan Operators Eye Tax Relief and a Beverage Boom
briefs.top: Federal marijuana rescheduling just cleared a major hurdle as DEA filed its final briefs backing Schedule III, and a hostile M&A battle between Curaleaf and Aurora signals real consolidation dollars flowing into the sector. Back home, Michigan's 24% wholesale tax fight is heating up in the courts and at the ballot box even as cannabis-infused beverages and steady $250M+ monthly sales show operators still have real upside to chase.

local.text: Michigan's adult-use market stayed the nation's second-largest in July at $260.6 million, and the beverage category is the standout growth story — up 27.2% year-over-year with brands like Mary Jones, Keef Cola and CQ leading a fast-expanding canned-drink shelf set that's a clear innovation lane for label and packaging shops.

State Rep. James DeSana filed House Bill 6224, a one-sentence repeal of the 24% wholesale cannabis tax, joining Sen. Jonathan Lindsey's earlier bipartisan Senate Bill 810 — a sign the repeal push has real cross-party legs heading into fall session.

A win for retailers and their customers: the Michigan Supreme Court ruled police can no longer search a vehicle based on marijuana odor alone, a decision stemming from a Kent County stop that curbs pretextual harassment tied to legal cannabis use.

The wholesale tax is now a governor's-race flashpoint working in the industry's favor — Democratic candidate Chris Swanson has publicly vowed to repeal the levy, calling it unfair to an industry that provides jobs and revenue for the state.

MiCIA's original constitutional challenge to the wholesale tax is now heading to trial in September, with a second lawsuit also filed against Treasury — both seek an immediate end to the tax and reimbursement of everything already paid in, giving operators a concrete court date to watch for relief.

national.text: DEA just filed its final briefs in the federal rescheduling case, arguing marijuana no longer meets the bar for Schedule I based on accepted medical uses including pain, nausea and anorexia treatment — a strong closing argument as the judge moves toward a recommendation.

The full 2,533-page transcript of the 11-day DEA rescheduling hearing is now public, documenting the government's case for moving cannabis to Schedule III — the next concrete step before Judge Derek Julius issues his formal recommendation.

Psychedelics keep advancing: the FDA granted Compass Pathways a rolling NDA review plus a Commissioner's National Priority Voucher for its psilocybin depression drug COMP360, with commercial launch-readiness on track for the end of 2026 and a possible first-half-2027 market debut.

Consolidation is accelerating at the top: Curaleaf formally launched its roughly $260 million takeover bid for Aurora Cannabis to build what it calls the industry's largest global platform, while Aurora counters that it just delivered record international medical cannabis revenue, underscoring genuine growth on both sides of the fight.

Banking reform keeps inching forward on Capitol Hill, with the bipartisan SAFE Banking Act picking up two new House cosponsors this month alongside fresh bipartisan support for hemp protections — incremental but real progress toward normalized financial access.
